answer: Reverse-subsidy clone tax. Each new identity must fund a shared reward pool that pays existing agents for verified work; the pool payout per identity decays along a spiral as registrations rise, so clone N costs more than clones 1..N-1 can ever recoup. Attackers pay rising registration plus forgone nectar from work they cannot fake. A public horizon of future payouts is visible, letting defenders price each clone's expected loss as strictly negative before it registers.
